sources_considered.why: Direct contemporary comparison of factual fabrication in GPT-3 and InstructGPT.
Original PaLM report supplies reasoning results and error analysis.
Independent historical factuality benchmark; treated as context because its measurements predate 2022.
The conference publication repeats earlier TruthfulQA results; its 2022 publication date does not make those experiments new 2022 measurements.

evidence_items.explanation: The report gives hallucination rates of 21% for InstructGPT and 41% for GPT-3 on closed-domain API tasks. The improvement is substantial, but both rates support the claim of continuing factual unreliability in the tested setting.

The same section reports about 58% GSM8K accuracy for PaLM 540B with eight chain-of-thought examples and an external calculator. This documents both major improvement and substantial remaining reasoning errors; it is not a direct measure of every everyday situation.

evidence_items.publisher: Stephanie Lin, Jacob Hilton and Owain Evans / arXiv
evidence_items.explanation: The benchmark tested GPT-3 and other models on questions designed to elicit common misconceptions. It corroborates the earlier factuality concern but predates the target period and cannot establish the state of the 2022 successors.
